new_statements.quote: The Bantoid sub-group Mambiloid comprises some 10 different languages of which Mambila. with at least 12 different dialects and over 100,000 speakers, is the largest; among the others are Kwanja, Ndoro, Vute, and Wawa, each of which also has dialectal variation, and Tep, Mbongo Mvanip, Ndunda, Somyev, and Nizaa, none of which is reported to have demonstrable dialectal variation. While for many of these the only data available are extended wordlists, most Mambiloid languages appear to have four contrastive lexical tones; Nizaa and Vute have three lexical tones, while one distinguishing feature among Mambila lects is three as opposed to four tones.

new_statements.relation_note: Mambiloid languages (Tep named) mostly have four contrastive lexical tones; Nizaa, Vute three; Mambila lects three or four; four-tone systems apparently evolved independently; Proto-Mambiloid tone reconstruction proposed. No Tep-specific figure and nothing on stress.
new_statements.rule_in_words: GROUP-LEVEL statement: the Mambiloid languages, Tep explicitly listed among them (known for several only from extended wordlists), are lexical (register) tone languages; 'most' have four contrastive lexical tones, the stated exceptions being Nizaa and Vute (three) and some Mambila lects (three vs four). Tep is not among the named exceptions but is not individually assigned a tone count. Nothing on stress/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Nizaa and Vute have three lexical tones; Mambila lects split three vs four; verb roots in Nizaa and Mambila contrast only two tones while nouns contrast three (Nizaa) or four (Mambila).
new_statements.identity_note: Conference abstract by the principal Mambiloid fieldworker; 'Tep' is enumerated among the ~10 Mambiloid languages alongside Mbongo, Mvanip, Ndunda, Somyev and Nizaa, i.e. Tep of Tep Kwar, Mambila Plateau (tepp1235; same author and same language set as Connell 2000/2001/2010 already held by the project). The tone-count sentence is group-level ('most Mambiloid languages'), with Tep not individually assigned a count; the named three-tone exceptions are Nizaa, Vute and some Mambila lects. The talk's slides/handout are not posted on the congress 'Presentations' page and no published version exists in Crossref (checked).
